values.value: Notes on the Model Context Protocol
Why giving AI agents a proper, typed handshake with your tools changes how we build.

documents.name: One Protocol to Connect Them All
documents.path: WWW / MCP Notes / One Protocol to Connect Them All

values.value: Before MCP, every AI integration was a bespoke adapter. Here is why a single open protocol for tools and context is such a big deal.

value.markup:
Anyone who has wired an AI assistant into a real system knows the pain: one custom adapter per tool, per model, per vendor. Every integration has its own auth story, its own schema dialect and its own way of failing. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) replaces that tangle with a single, open contract.

Write a tool once, use it everywhere

An MCP server describes what it can do: the tools it offers, the shape of their inputs, and the resources it can expose. Any MCP-capable client can discover that description at runtime and start using it. Build the server once and it works with every compliant agent, editor and chat app, today and tomorrow.

values.value: Standard plumbing beats a drawer full of one-off adapters.
USB-C did not make devices smarter. It made them interchangeable, and that is what let an ecosystem grow.
A common way to explain MCP

value.markup:
Typed, discoverable and safe by design

Because tools are described with JSON Schema, the agent knows exactly which arguments are required and what comes back. That means fewer hallucinated parameters and clearer errors. The server stays in control of what is exposed, so you decide which capabilities an agent gets, and which it never sees.

The ecosystem is the feature

Databases, issue trackers, design tools, CMSs: each new MCP server makes every existing client more capable, and each new client makes every server more valuable. That network effect is why MCP is awesome.

documents.name: Building a CMS Site by Conversation
documents.path: WWW / MCP Notes / Building a CMS Site by Conversation

values.value: With an MCP server in front of Umbraco, an agent can model, populate and publish content through the same management API the backoffice uses.

value.markup:
This entire site, its document types, data types, media and content, was built by an AI agent talking to a running Umbraco instance over MCP. No clicking through the backoffice, no hand-edited database rows. Just tool calls.

Model first, then content

The agent starts by inspecting what already exists, then creates element types for each block, block grid data types that allow them, and the page types that host them. Every step goes through Umbraco's own management API, so validation, permissions and the folder conventions of the project all still apply.

values.value: The agent works against a live site, not a mock of it.
The best integration is the one you did not have to write.

value.markup:
Content, media and publishing

Once the schema exists, the same server uploads images straight from a URL, creates documents with block grid values, assigns domains and publishes. Read-backs confirm the payload landed the way it was intended.

Why it matters

Editors and developers get a shared, scriptable surface. Repetitive setup becomes a conversation, and the CMS stays the single source of truth. That is MCP doing what it does best: turning a product's capabilities into tools an agent can use safely.
